metadata.name: pleiades-core-epistemic-distinctions
metadata.notes: Initial executable registry for distinctions whose collapse repeatedly degrades reasoning across clinical, institutional, and systems domains.

terms.label: Deliberate
terms.description: An action, policy, framing, or repeated choice selected intentionally by an actor or institution.

terms.label: Conspiratorial
terms.description: Secret or concealed coordination among multiple actors toward a shared plan.

middleSpace.label: Distributed institutional intention
middleSpace.description: Multiple institutions make deliberate local choices that interact without a single hidden command structure.

middleSpace.label: Parallel incentive alignment
middleSpace.description: Actors independently select similar strategies because their incentives and constraints converge.

forbiddenCollapses.reason: Intentional conduct does not imply centralized or secret multi-party coordination.
Conspiracy is a narrower coordination claim, not a synonym for intentional action.

competencyQuestions: Can the system represent intentional institutional action without asserting secret centralized coordination?
Can the system identify the actors, local decisions, incentives, and interaction effects separately?
Can the system distinguish evidence of intent from evidence of coordination?

counterexamples.label: Independent price matching
counterexamples.description: Firms can intentionally match a market strategy after observing one another without entering a secret agreement.

counterexamples.label: Distributed administrative framing
counterexamples.description: Agencies and media organizations can deliberately emphasize compatible narratives through separate institutional incentives.

terms.label: Behavioral description
terms.description: Language naming an observable pattern, strategy, or functional resemblance.

terms.label: Clinical diagnosis
terms.description: A formal clinical classification requiring defined criteria, history, context, and assessment.

middleSpace.label: Dimensional trait description
middleSpace.description: A graded description of traits that does not assert a categorical disorder.

middleSpace.label: Functional analogy
middleSpace.description: A comparison between behavior at one scale and a clinical pattern without diagnosing an individual.

forbiddenCollapses.reason: Descriptive language does not by itself establish a disorder.
A diagnosis is not an exhaustive description of a person's motives, capacities, or conduct.

competencyQuestions: Can the system preserve a behavioral descriptor without silently converting it into a diagnostic assertion?
Can the system state when clinical criteria are relevant without allowing the taxonomy to monopolize ordinary language?
Can it represent mixed empathic and strategic traits without forcing a fixed personality type?

counterexamples.label: Situational Machiavellian strategy
counterexamples.description: A highly empathic person may use strategic concealment in a constrained situation without having a personality disorder.

counterexamples.label: Institutional sociopathic phenotype
counterexamples.description: An organization may behave with systematic callousness even when no individual member meets a clinical construct.

terms.label: Trait
terms.description: A dimensional tendency that may vary by degree, context, and time.

terms.label: Disorder
terms.description: A clinically significant pattern meeting a diagnostic framework's requirements for dysfunction or impairment.

middleSpace.label: Subclinical cluster
middleSpace.description: A recognizable configuration of traits below or outside a disorder threshold.

middleSpace.label: Role-amplified trait
middleSpace.description: A tendency made more visible by incentives, authority, stress, or institutional position.

forbiddenCollapses.reason: Possessing a trait does not imply categorical pathology.
A disorder classification includes severity, persistence, and functional context beyond a single trait.

competencyQuestions: Can the ontology represent degree and context without inventing a categorical boundary?
Can it distinguish role-amplified conduct from enduring personality structure?
Can it retain uncertainty around thresholds?

counterexamples.label: Empathic manipulation under duress
counterexamples.description: A person can manipulate while retaining guilt, attachment, affective empathy, and moral concern.

counterexamples.label: Low-impairment dark-triad traits
counterexamples.description: Subclinical trait measures need not imply the severe stereotype attached to a disorder label.

terms.label: Deliberate confusion
terms.description: Intentional structuring of salience, categories, or attention that predictably impairs accurate understanding.

terms.label: Deception
terms.description: Conduct intended to cause acceptance of a materially false belief.

middleSpace.label: Selective truth framing
middleSpace.description: True facts are disproportionately foregrounded while qualifications and countervailing facts remain technically available.

middleSpace.label: Salience engineering
middleSpace.description: Attention is steered through repetition, emotional association, ordering, and category choice.

forbiddenCollapses.reason: Confusion may be produced without fabricating or concealing a specific material fact.
Direct falsehood is a more specific mechanism than general epistemic distortion.

competencyQuestions: Can the system identify misleading salience while acknowledging that the cited facts are individually true?
Can it distinguish audience effect from the actor's exact false-belief objective?
Can it preserve public availability of contrary evidence as a relevant but non-exculpatory fact?

counterexamples.label: Technically complete report
counterexamples.description: A report can disclose contrary data in an appendix while headlines and summaries produce a strongly distorted interpretation.

counterexamples.label: Direct fabrication
counterexamples.description: Inventing a nonexistent event is deception even if the audience is not broadly confused about the surrounding topic.

terms.label: Emergence
terms.description: A higher-order pattern arising from interactions among components, possibly including deliberate local actions.

terms.label: Accident
terms.description: An outcome not selected or intended by the relevant actor at the relevant level of analysis.

middleSpace.label: Intended locally, emergent globally
middleSpace.description: Components act deliberately while the aggregate pattern is not centrally designed.

middleSpace.label: Anticipated emergence
middleSpace.description: Actors expect a system-level effect and continue contributing without controlling the whole process.

forbiddenCollapses.reason: An emergent result may contain intentional local causes and may be anticipated.
Not every unintended event is a stable higher-order interaction pattern.

competencyQuestions: Can the system assign intention separately at component and system levels?
Can it represent an emergent outcome that was anticipated but not centrally controlled?
Can it distinguish a one-off mishap from a recurrent interaction pattern?

counterexamples.label: Traffic congestion
counterexamples.description: Drivers intentionally select routes while congestion emerges without any driver intending the full traffic pattern.

counterexamples.label: Algorithmic feedback loop
counterexamples.description: Teams deliberately optimize local metrics and knowingly sustain a global feedback effect they do not centrally orchestrate.

terms.label: Consensus
terms.description: Agreement or convergence among agents, institutions, or sources.

terms.label: Evidence
terms.description: Observations, measurements, records, tests, or arguments that bear on a proposition.

middleSpace.label: Evidence-weighted convergence
middleSpace.description: Agreement produced after independent evidence-bearing contributions are compared.

middleSpace.label: Coordinated consensus
middleSpace.description: Agreement caused partly by shared incentives, copied priors, communication topology, or authority pressure.

forbiddenCollapses.reason: Agreement is not itself proof and may reflect correlated error.
Strong evidence can exist before or despite social agreement.

competencyQuestions: Can the system measure source independence rather than merely count agreeing agents?
Can it preserve minority evidence and confidence when a majority converges?
Can it distinguish copied conclusions from independently derived support?

counterexamples.label: Homogeneous model vote
counterexamples.description: Ten instances sharing the same training and prompt can repeat one correlated mistake.

counterexamples.label: Single decisive measurement
counterexamples.description: A high-quality instrument reading can outweigh broad opinion lacking direct evidence.
